concerns.text: T015b and T015c treat real data ingestion as a conditional override or CI fallback. FR-002 mandates 'capture' of transient-absorption data. The tasks do not implement the 'capture' mechanism (instrument interface) required by the spec, only file ingestion or synthetic generation. This silently weakens the FR-002 requirement to 'file processing' rather than 'data capture'.

Spec Edge Cases require the system to 'pause experiment and alert researcher' when humidity/temperature tolerances are breached. T014 and T041 only implement logging and flagging. No task implements the active control loop (pausing/halting) required by the spec's acceptance criteria for edge cases.

FR-005 requires explicit solvent models (QM/MM or cluster-continuum) for ≥20% of conditions. T029a fetches DFT data (implicit) and T029b partitions the list. No task exists to generate, fetch, or validate the 'explicit' QM/MM data required to satisfy the 20% constraint. The deliverable falls short of the FR.

SC-007 requires a documented power analysis. T059 outputs a JSON with a hardcoded default effect size (0.8) and explicitly defers effect size estimation. A document relying on a placeholder without a mechanism to update it upon effect size determination fails to be a valid scientific record as required by the spec's deferment convention (which requires naming the metric, not just the placeholder).

T017a raises a `ConfigurationError` and halts the pipeline if `state/artifact_hashes.yaml` is missing. The spec requires a robust system that handles configuration states gracefully. Hard-crashing on missing state artifacts (which can happen in fresh environments) violates the robustness implied by the acceptance criteria for environmental validation.
